issues.ko: 문이 3개(1~3번) 있고, 그중 한 문 뒤에만 자동차가 있다. 자동차는 처음에 모든 문 뒤에 같은 확률로 놓인다. 참가자가 문 하나를 고르면 사회자가 참가자가 고르지 않은 문 1개를 연다. 사회자는 자동차가 어느 문 뒤에 있는지 안다. 참가자가 처음에 자동차가 있는 문을 골랐을 때만, 고르지 않은 문 가운데 1개를 무작위로(가능한 조합이 모두 같은 확률로) 골라 열어 준다. 참가자가 빈 문을 골랐으면 사회자는 문을 하나도 열지 않고 곧바로 참가자가 고른 문을 열어 게임을 끝낸다. 문이 열린 뒤 참가자는 처음 고른 문을 그대로 두거나 아직 닫힌 다른 문 하나로 바꿀 수 있고, 마지막에 고른 문 뒤의 것을 받는다.
issues.en: There are 3 doors (numbered 1~3), and a car is behind only one of them. At the start, the car is placed behind each door with the same probability. When the contestant picks one door, the host opens 1 door the contestant did not pick. The host knows which door the car is behind. Only when the contestant initially picked the door with the car does the host choose 1 at random (with every possible combination having the same probability) from among the doors not picked and open it. If the contestant picked an empty door, the host, without opening a single door, immediately opens the door the contestant picked and ends the game. After the doors are opened, the contestant may stay with the originally picked door or switch to one other door that is still closed, and receives what is behind the door picked in the end.
issues.explanation: '문이 열린 뒤' is number-neutral; 'After the doors are opened' is plural even in rules where the host opens 1 door. The count is stated just before ('opens 1 door'), so nobody will infer more doors; keeping the shared sentence identical across the twin rules is worth more than agreement. No change needed.

issues.ko: 참가자가 2번 문을 골랐다. 사회자가 3번 문을 열었고, 연 문 뒤는 모두 비어 있었다. 아직 닫힌 문은 1, 2번이다.
issues.en: The contestant picked door 2. The host opened door 3, and nothing was behind any of the opened doors. The doors still closed are doors 1 and 2.
issues.explanation: Korean says '모두 비어 있었다' even for one door, so 'nothing was behind any of the opened doors' is a fair mirror; 'nothing was behind' vs the rules' 'empty doors' is a wording difference with the same meaning. No change needed.
